summary: This listing adds two number-crunching helper methods to the farmers' market app: one that converts each product's price into a stream of doubles and totals them, and one that keeps only the organic products before averaging their prices.

lines.text: This placeholder stands in for the product list built in the earlier farmers' market exercises; the printed listing focuses only on the new calculations, so the list is assumed to already exist here.
The heavy lifting lives in a named helper method, which keeps main readable and lets the same calculation be reused elsewhere.
String.format with "%.2f" rounds the double to two decimal places so the money value reads like a price instead of something like 25.449999999999996.
The method returns a plain double, so callers get a finished number and never have to know a stream was involved.
mapToDouble turns the stream of products into a DoubleStream of prices, which unlocks numeric operations that a general object stream does not offer.
sum is a terminal operation available only on primitive streams like DoubleStream, and it returns 0.0 for an empty list rather than failing.
Filtering before mapping keeps only the organic products, so the average is computed from that subset alone.
average returns an OptionalDouble rather than a double, because there is no meaningful average when no product passes the filter.
orElse supplies a fallback value when the Optional is empty, which avoids an exception if the market has no organic items.
